title: jobs
definition: A command that lists the active jobs (background processes) that have been started by, and are attached to, your current terminal session.
simpleExplanation: Checking what tasks are running invisibly behind the scenes in your current window.
realWorldExample: You start a massive database backup. It takes 30 minutes. You pause it with `Ctrl+Z`, then type `bg` to send it to the background so you can keep typing. You type `jobs` to see a numbered list verifying the backup is still running invisibly.

basic: Will the `jobs` command show a background process started by another user on the server?
intermediate: How do you bring a background job (like job number 2) back to the foreground so you can interact with it?

answers.question: Show other users' jobs?
answers.answer: No. `jobs` ONLY shows processes tied specifically to your exact current terminal window.

answers.question: Bring to foreground?
answers.answer: Use the `fg` (foreground) command followed by the job number: `fg %2`.
